text:
eli_acme: Hey team, our service api.acme.com started returning NXDOMAIN from our private VPC today. Public DNS resolves fine from my laptop. This started after we onboarded the Redwood private deployment. Anyone seen this before?

sara_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a quick dig/nslookup output from a host in the failing VPC? Also which AWS account/VPC is the app running in?

eli_acme: Sure, from an app node in subnet-0a1b2c3d:```$ dig +short api.acme.com @169.254.169.253 ;; -> no output, NXDOMAIN on lookup``` We're in acct: 111122223333 VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (dev).

raj_eng: Two quick things to check: 1) Do you have a Route53 private hosted zone for acme.com in any AWS account? 2) Are there Resolver rules or inbound endpoints in the account that could be stealing queries? Run:```aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query "HostedZones[?Config.PrivateZone==true]" --output json``` and```aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <zoneid>``` to see VPC associations.

eli_acme: Ran the list. Output showed a private hosted zone for acme.com but in a different account (222233334444). I guess automation spun it up there. get-hosted-zone shows it's associated only with vpc-0b2c3d4e in that account.

morgan_sre: That sounds like a split-horizon collision — a private hosted zone with the same name in a different account won't resolve in your dev VPC unless associated. But if you have an outbound resolver rule in your account forwarding to central resolver, or resolver rules with higher priority, it can cause NXDOMAIN if the query gets forwarded to a zone without a record. Check your VPC's resolver rules:```aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d``` Also check default route53 resolver behavior and any conditional forwarders.

route53-bot: [automated] Hosted zone acme.com (private) detected in account 222233334444 not associated with VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d. No overlapping records found in account 111122223333.

raj_eng: If the private zone exists in another account and the central resolver is forwarding to that account but the zone doesn't have the expected records, queries can end up NXDOMAIN. Two remediation paths: A) Associate the correct private hosted zone with your VPC (if ownership is intended), B) Delete the stray private zone or update the forwarding rules so your VPC queries go to the public resolver for acme.com. Which one matches your org setup?

eli_acme: We want the public records (we're multi-tenant). The private zone in 2222 account was created by a partner by mistake. Can we force queries to public again?

morgan_sre: Yes — quick test: from your VPC namespace run dig against 8.8.8.8 and the VPC resolver to confirm difference:```dig +short api.acme.com @8.8.8.8``` and ```dig +short api.acme.com @169.254.169.253``` If 8.8.8.8 returns the public A record and VPC resolver returns NXDOMAIN, then it's definitely a private hosted zone shadowing issue via resolver/forwarding.

eli_acme: Test results: 8.8.8.8 -> 3.14.159.26; VPC resolver -> NXDOMAIN.

raj_eng: Ok confirm. Short-term unblock: remove the conditional forwarder/Resolver rule that sends acme.com to the partner account (or set rule priority lower). Longer term: either have the partner delete their private hosted zone or agree to associate their hosted zone with your VPC (if internal records are required). I'll open an internal RFC with DNS team to prevent cross-account private-zone creation without tagging.

eli_acme: I've asked partner to delete the private zone. Meanwhile I removed the resolver rule and my service started resolving:```dig +short api.acme.com @169.254.169.253 -> 3.14.159.26``` All good now, thanks. :tada:

sara_support: Great — filing a follow-up ticket to add a check in our onboarding playbook to validate no overlapping private hosted zones exist and to surface resolver-rule changes. Marking thread resolved but ping if it reappears. :white_check_mark:
